reference_traces.rationale: The reviewer identified the flexible pendant-linker design as the informative contribution. The final paper describes APBA's rotatable C–N bond and presents the APBA/BCA comparison and calculated binding energies.

The reviewer characterized the work as tethering a known ligand-supported Pd(II) catalyst in a MOF and as an incremental, rather than ground-breaking, advance. The final paper likewise positions the work amid established MOF modification and single-atom-catalyst approaches.

The reviewer considered the characterization sufficient to support a proposed coordination environment. The final paper reports microscopy, elemental mapping, XPS, and EXAFS evidence for dispersed Pd coordinated to APBA.

The reviewer described the catalysis experiments as reasonably comprehensive and noted the use of controls. The final paper reports a three-repeat averaged TON and the MOF-808 and molecular Pd-MAPB control results.

The reviewer queried the observed Pd agglomeration. The response explains it as Pd(0) nanoparticle formation, and the final paper confirms nanoparticles after recycling; APBA is supported as delaying, not preventing, agglomeration.

The reviewer requested stronger post-catalysis evidence that molecular Pd complexes remain rather than only small nanoparticles. The response and final paper add post-reaction XPS, but the final paper also documents nanoparticle formation and does not report the requested repeat EXAFS/XANES measurement.
The requested TON definition and repeated averaging are supported in the final paper: TON is defined as product-to-catalyst molar ratio and the reported high TON is an average of three repeats.
The final paper reports MOF-808 and molecular Pd-MAPB controls and quantifies BCA incorporation per Zr6 cluster, addressing the requested controls and linker-loading information.
The response states that Fig. 3e and 3f were replaced with more intuitive depictions, and the final paper contains the corresponding optimized complex structures and caption.
The final introduction cites the antecedent APBA ligand core and literature on flexibility during metalation and coordination.

The response states that synthetic conditions and proton assignments were added in the Supporting Information, but the supplied final-paper spans do not independently expose those detailed Supporting Information records.
The response states that the introduction was reconfigured; the final paper presents a focused introduction linking MOF functionalization, linker flexibility, and APBA design.

limiting_points.suggested_action: Frame the advance as a ligand-design and stabilization insight within established MOF-supported palladium catalysis.
limiting_points.text: The conceptual advance is bounded by prior MOF-supported and ligand-supported Pd catalysis: the distinctive element is the flexible APBA pendant linker rather than the general heterogenization strategy.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Retain the comparison that connects APBA flexibility to Pd stabilization.
supporting_points.text: The flexible N,N′-bidentate APBA linker supplies a specific design insight: its rotatable C–N bond is proposed to improve Pd coordination relative to the BCA analogue and accommodate changing coordination environments.

questions.suggested_action: Measure the spent catalyst with a coordination-sensitive method, such as repeat EXAFS/XANES, and quantify the retained molecular Pd fraction alongside nanoparticle formation.
questions.text: What fraction and coordination environment of Pd remains as anchored molecular complexes after catalysis? Post-reaction XPS supports residual Pd(II), while TEM/HRTEM also show Pd nanoparticles after recycling.

strengths.text: Complementary TEM/HRTEM, HAADF-STEM/EDS, XPS, and EXAFS evidence supports APBA coordination of Pd and dispersed Pd species before catalysis.

The catalytic assessment includes a three-repeat averaged high-TON measurement and informative controls: MOF-808 gives no product and the molecular Pd-MAPB complex is less favourable on the reported metric.

summary.text: The study replaces the MOF-808 modulator ligand with APBA to anchor palladium for Heck catalysis. It reports a flexible bidentate coordination design, comparison with a BCA analogue, atomically dispersed Pd before reaction, an averaged TON above 95,000, and recycling evidence. The review record supports this as a useful but bounded ligand-design contribution, with post-catalysis Pd speciation and agglomeration remaining the central residual evidence gap.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Qualify stability claims to distinguish delayed agglomeration from its prevention and report the associated loss of molecularly dispersed Pd.
weaknesses.text: Pd nanoparticles are present after recycling, including an average 11.66 nm size for Pd@MOF-APBA. The evidence supports delayed agglomeration relative to Pd@MOF-808, but not complete suppression of agglomeration.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: The final paper defines TON and reports three-repeat averaging; no retained residual issue.
MOF and molecular-complex controls and BCA linker incorporation are reported; no retained residual issue.
The response describes revised Fig. 3e–f depictions and the final paper provides the optimized-complex caption.
The requested antecedent-linker and flexible-MOF context is cited in the final introduction.
The response locates detailed synthesis and NMR assignments in Supporting Information, but those details cannot be verified from the supplied final-paper spans.
The final introduction presents the field context and rationale for APBA design.
